liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Reuben and Cherise** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out Reuben and Cherise as a cool moment, though not a standout show overall; Reuben and Cherise called rare and probably the best ever [12][14][25]
- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Sugaree and Minglewood both described as nice; Bruce's presence is said to liven up the band; Sugaree has a dueling-banjos quality, with the trading of leads between players [13][21]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Jerry uses a horn-like sound on Ramble On Rose, giving a trippy, midi-flavored groove [21]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 review): Samson and Delilah gave a nice kick into the second set [14]
- **He's Gone** (1 other source): Uploader says He's Gone is a transporting version [7]
- **The Other One** (1 other source): Jerry adds a violin-like effect to the intro of The Other One [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Reuben and Cherise**: rare: 5 archived performances [24]

## The recordings

- **gd91-06-09.sbd.unknown.12756.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 168 min; rated 3.83/5 by 36 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is awesome, but the Wharf Rat intro is cut, and disc 2 track 7 has only 16 seconds of Space before The Other One [16]
- **gd1991-06-09.140670.FOB.Schoeps.unknown.Ammons.Noel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 17 songs; 172 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [7]
- **gd1991-06-09.140238.TS.beyercm101.ebel.flac1644**: source not stated; 17 songs; 168 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [8]
- **gd1991-06-09.fob.brennecke-young.GEMS.95641.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 170 min; rated 4.67/5 by 9 [2]

## Around the show

- Seating was general admission with a rush for spots; the Violent Femmes opened, starting with a small acoustic setup in front of the Dead's gear [12]
- Gordon Gano's voice from the Violent Femmes pierced through the speaker stacks before the Dead came on [22]
- It rained much of the day; reviewer mentions lights going out during the show and the next stop being Pine Bluff [23]
- Reviewer says 1991 was not the best Buckeye Lake show ever, but still stands out among them [14]
- Bruce's contributions suit the focused first-set songs more than the stretched-out second-set jams of this era [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-06-09.sbd.unknown.12756.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> DAT> CD> SHN [1]. Also: Soundboard source transferred from DAT to CD to SHN; provenance unknown, submitted by user kberry [1]
- **gd1991-06-09.140670.FOB.Schoeps.unknown.Ammons.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Unknown; transferred by John Ammons and Joe Noel; source: flac16/48 ; taper unknown: FOB Schoeps CMC32s spaced 8 ft > Tao Research PS > M1000 cables > Panasonic SV255 with 6'3" stands; John Ammons [7]. Also: Schoeps microphone recording; hand claps removed, and in set 2 DC offset was removed and only the left channel normalized [7]
- **gd1991-06-09.140238.TS.beyercm101.ebel.flac1644**: taped by Pete Ebel; transferred by Pete Ebel; source: flac16/44 Source Info: TS Beyer CM 101-> Sony D6-> Cassette Master (Maxell XL-II's 90's). Transfer Info: Master Cassette-> Nakamichi CR-5A -> Grace Lunatec V3… [8]. Also: Beyerdynamic-mic taper source; gaps at tape flips after Ramble On Rose and during Drumz were filled with audio from GEMS 95642 [8]
- **gd1991-06-09.fob.brennecke-young.GEMS.95641.flac16**: taped by James Young and Clay Brennecke; transferred by Todd Evans and Jamie Waddell; source: B&K 4011 110 degrees ORTF > Neumann BS 48i-2> Modified Sony TCD D-10 Pro , Recording Location: DFC Front Row Taper Section [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Michael: [1991-06-09 Buckeye Lake Music Center, Hebron, OH, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1991-06-09-buckeye-lake-music-center-hebron-oh-usa/) [26]
